key_insight: A hybrid nanocone-plus-nanohole silicon architecture improves light trapping by reducing front reflection and increasing internal optical confinement, boosting thin-film solar-cell efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This design offers a practical nanostructuring strategy to raise current generation and maintain performance in thin-film silicon photovoltaics under realistic thermal conditions.
method: Added front-surface silicon nanocones to create a gradual refractive-index transition.
Embedded air-filled nanoholes in the absorber to increase scattering and internal reflection.
Optimized geometry and doping with FDTD coupled to electrical and opto-electro-thermal simulations.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, while retaining 95.21% efficiency up to 45°C.
watch_item: The architecture relies on precise nanoscale fabrication and model assumptions, so experimental manufacturability and defect sensitivity need validation.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
